summary: Backend engineer with five years building payment and ledger services for fintech companies. Currently owns the settlement pipeline of a card-issuing platform: Go services on PostgreSQL, Kafka between them, Kubernetes underneath. Likes boring technology, explicit error handling and tests that fail for a reason. Spends personal time on a small open-source rate limiter and on learning Rust.

headline.label: card-issuing platform, first commit to launch

blocks.title: Card-issuing platform — settlement and ledger
bullets: Own the settlement pipeline end to end: Go services, PostgreSQL with strict double-entry constraints, Kafka for the event flow between issuing, clearing and reporting.
Took throughput from 40 to 4,000 requests per second by batching writes, partitioning the ledger and moving reconciliation off the request path.
Wrote the team's runbooks and the incident review template; on-call rotation lead for two quarters.
Mentor two junior engineers; run a weekly design review.
Built the merchant payouts service (Go, PostgreSQL, gRPC) and its reconciliation jobs against three acquiring banks.
Introduced contract tests between services; cut integration incidents by half over a year.
Maintained the internal admin tool (TypeScript, React) and the nightly reporting jobs.

projects.title: ratelimit-go
projects.summary: A small, dependency-free token-bucket rate limiter for Go with a Redis-backed mode. Used in production by two companies I know of.

projects.title: Double-entry ledger kata
projects.summary: The same ledger implemented in Go, Rust and PostgreSQL-only, with one property-based test suite proving they agree. A learning project.
